reply.question: When was the checkout queue longest, how many tills were open then, roughly how many customers arrived per minute and how long did each take to serve? Do we need another till?
reply.answer:
Longest checkout queue in the recording was at ~01:13:07 UTC on 4 Nov on the checkout-queue camera (phone-15) facing the Card-only / self-checkout tills:

- 22 customers present in view at 01:13:07.623Z. Next largest was 21 at 01:03:10Z on phone-11.
- Tills open then: 2 of 2 tills open and serving. Tracker saw 3-5 cashier tracks at the facing front-end tills (phone-14) around 01:13:07-01:13:09 (3 at 01:13:07, rising to 4-5), but visually only 2 lanes were actively serving the queue - the foreground lane and the lane to its left - confirmed by look and by the retail check: `6 waiting, 2 of 2 tills open; about 240s wait; open another till` at 01:10:53Z.
- Arrivals: ~6 customers per minute. Watch of phone-15 01:12:00-01:13:00 saw 2 new trolley shoppers join per ~20s = 5-7/min, queue 2 longer at end than start. Track starts also peak at 01:12 with 122 new customer fragments that minute (over-counts fragments, same trend).
- Serve time: ~60-90 sec per customer per till, typically ~1 minute. No completion seen in ~20s of watching, consistent with 240s wait for 6 waiting on 2 tills = ~80s each.

Do we need another till? Yes. Arrivals ~6/min ≈ capacity of 2 tills at ~1/min each (~2/min total served if 2 open, 6-8/min if all 6-8 positions busy but only 2 staffed), so queue was stable to slowly growing. System already raised `Please open another till to help the checkout queue` (alert al-2). Open a 3rd till.

How got: max COUNT(DISTINCT track_id) per ts for concept customer on queue cameras, cashier counts on till cameras at same ts, retail_findings queue checks, verified by look at 01:13:07 and 60s watch. Medium-high confidence - track counts at an instant are reliable, arrival/service are rough visual estimates.

steps.thought: Find when checkout queue cameras had most customers present.
Get average dwell/service time proxy from track spans.
Check till cameras for open tills and long customer stays.
Check tills open at peak, arrivals per minute, and queue findings.
Visually verify queue length and open tills at the 22-person peak.
Check front-end tills facing the same peak for open count.
Estimate arrival rate and service time from motion.
Peak is 22 at 01:13:07 with 2 tills open, arrivals ~6/min, ~1 min serve, needs another till.

answer.question: ¿Cuántos clientes esperaban en las cajas y cuántas cajas estaban abiertas?
answer.answer:
A las ~01:19:40 UTC (último video grabado):

- Checkout queue (phone-19, vista amplia): ~9 clientes esperando en la cola + 1-2 ya en mostrador pagando = 10-11 clientes en zona de cajas. Se ven 2 cajas abiertas con cajero atendiendo.
- Checkout lanes (phone-17): se ven 3 mostradores, 2 en uso, con 2 clientes esperando en la cola del carril central.
- Front-end tills (phone-18): se ven 3-4 mostradores amarillos, 2 abiertos con cajero/a de camisa verde, con 1 cliente pagando y 1 esperando + 1 acercándose con carrito.

Las 3 cámaras miran la misma zona frontal desde ángulos distintos, por lo que no se suman: en total hay unas 9 personas en cola + 2-3 en caja y 2 cajas abiertas atendiendo. No hay cola larga desbordada, escena tranquila. Obtenido por inspección visual de los 3 encuadres a las 01:19:40-42, confianza media.

ask1.question: When was the checkout queue longest, how many tills were open then, roughly how many customers arrived per minute and how long did each take to serve? Do we need another till?
ask1.answer:
Longest recorded checkout queue was at ~00:44:27 UTC on 4 Nov (checkout lanes camera phone-1): 5 customers waiting, with 3 of 3 tills open, estimated ~180s (3 min) wait. That is the only queue finding in the recording (00:20-00:48), so it is the peak we can see.

Tills open then: 3 of 3 open - i.e. all available tills were staffed/serving. No extra till to open without adding capacity.

Arrivals and service: video from 00:41:27-00:44:27 on the checkout-queue camera is a short ~20-36s loop repeated, so true throughput cannot be measured reliably. Rough visual estimate was ~5-6 new shoppers joining per minute and ~60-120s per till transaction (typically ~45-90s scanning + payment, ~2 min with bagging). Confidence low because of the loop.

Do you need another till? On this evidence: not yet actioned by the system (act=false, no task opened), but you are at capacity. 5 waiting with all 3 tills open and ~3 min wait is at the usual supermarket threshold (open another till at >3-4 waiting or >2-3 min wait). If arrivals stay at ~5/min, you will need a 4th till / staffed express lane or to divert to self-scan, otherwise the queue will grow.

How I got it: retail_findings queue check + visual check of phone-1/phone-3 video. Sure on queue length/tills (system finding); arrival/service rates are rough and low-confidence due to looped video and no track/crowd data.

voice1.transcript: ¿Cuántos clientes esperaban en las cajas y cuántas cajas estaban abiertas?.?

answer.question: ¿Cuántos clientes esperaban en las cajas y cuántas cajas estaban abiertas?.?
answer.answer:
A las 00:59:50 UTC del 04/11/2026:
- Clientes esperando en la zona de checkout queue (cámara phone-11): 17 personas detectadas por conteo automático. En las vistas de tills/lanes (phone-10 y phone-9) se detectaron 7 personas en cada una, compatibles con clientes en cajas y en cola.
- Cajas abiertas: al menos 3 mostradores de caja visibles/detectados en front-end tills (phone-10) y 2 en checkout lanes (phone-9), por lo que estimo unas 3 cajas operativas.

Cómo lo obtuve: conteo automático SAM 3.1 de `person` y `checkout counter` sobre los fotogramas grabados de phone-9, phone-10 y phone-11 a las 00:59:50 UTC. La verificación visual con Muse Glimmer (look) falló por timeout y no hay captions ni retail_findings para ese minuto, por lo que la cifra de cajas abiertas es de confianza media-baja y la de clientes en espera es conteo de personas en la zona de cola, no distinción perfecta cliente/personal.

brief1.text: Las cajas estuvieron ocupadas con un pico de 9 personas esperando. Se pidieron 2 aperturas de caja y se mandaron 3 avisos con 0 respuestas. En estantería hay 11 huecos, unos 152 frentes por reponer, con 2 tareas abiertas y 0 terminadas. En el suelo hay 1 derrame confirmado de leche, riesgo alto de caída. Usted preguntó cuándo fue la cola más larga y si hace falta otra caja. El registro habla de las 00:44 con 3 de 3 cajas abiertas. La prueba de abrir una cuarta caja sigue midiendo, con 0 de 6 pares hechos y 1 lectura media de 9. Aún es pronto para saber. Hay que decidir abrir otra caja y limpiar y reponer. Las cámaras no vieron otros pasillos ni llegadas por minuto.
